findings.mechanism: Allah is the nominative subject of the completed favor verb and is followed by the dual recipient phrase, so the favor has a stated agent rather than an anonymous source.
findings.reader_payoff: The two speakers' authority is introduced as grounded in named divine agency.
findings.containment: The finding stays within the supplied favor clause and does not infer a broader authorization beyond that agency relation.

epistemic.reason: QAC case and attachment evidence directly establish the subject relation.

findings.title: dual favor recipient
findings.claim: The dual upon-phrase targets the completed favor specifically to the two named speakers.
findings.mechanism: The attached dual suffix agrees with the dual subject and functions under the favor verb, restricting the recipient frame before the quotation opens.
findings.reader_payoff: Favor is grammatically focused on the two who will speak, rather than diffused across the fearful group.
findings.containment: The finding specifies the supplied recipient relation and does not deny favor to anyone outside the clause's explicit frame.

epistemic.reason: The supplied suffix and attachment rows directly support the dual recipient relation.

findings.title: collective entry command

findings.mechanism: Its second-person plural morphology shares the audience with the later promise, while the adversarial complement and definite gate give the command both target and threshold.
findings.reader_payoff: The speakers do more than offer morale: they turn refusal into a collective demanded act.
findings.containment: The finding keeps the command's ordinary addressees and physical entry visible without inferring that the command has already been obeyed.

epistemic.reason: QAC imperative morphology and the supplied attachment evidence establish the commanded audience and complements.
